scenes.text: From a screening in a Paris cafe to films streamed into your living room: six turns in movie history.
In 1895, the Lumiere brothers showed their films to a paying audience in Paris.
In 1927, The Jazz Singer brought synchronized spoken dialogue to a feature film.
In 1935, Becky Sharp became the first feature shot entirely in three-strip Technicolor.
In 1977, Star Wars turned the summer blockbuster into a worldwide event.
In 1995, Pixar's Toy Story became the first fully computer-animated feature film.
And in 2007, Netflix began streaming films over the internet.
